text: P166685 - Uganda Electricity Access Scale-up Project (EASP).
Objective: to increase access to energy for households, commercial enterprises, industrial parks and public institutions; unchanged since approval (ISR p. 1).
Implementing agencies: Ministry of Energy and Mineral Development (MEMD) and Uganda Energy Credit Capitalisation Company (UECCC) (Projects record; ISR p. 1). Borrower: Republic of Uganda.

Commitment: IDA US$568 million (credit IDA-70750 US$331.5 million and grant IDA-D9970 US$236.5 million), plus trust-fund grants (CTF US$30 million, ESMAP US$10 million); total project cost US$638 million including private sector and government contributions (Projects record; ISR p. 15). The commitment is the World Bank financing, not the total project cost.
Dates: approved 31 March 2022, signed 20 February 2023, effective 20 July 2023; closing 30 June 2027 (ISR p. 16). Midterm review held 7 November 2025 (p. 16).

Latest public implementation update: ISR seq. 10, 14 August 2026. Progress towards the PDO Moderately Satisfactory; implementation progress downgraded from Moderately Satisfactory to Moderately Unsatisfactory; overall risk Substantial, with sector strategies and institutional capacity rated High and fiduciary raised to High (pp. 1-2). Results: 612,757 connections against a 1,571,500 target (155,088 grid connections by Umeme, 44,826 by UEDCL, 412,843 off-grid); 873,848 people with clean cooking against 1,660,000; 284 public institutions against 700 (pp. 3-4). Disbursement: 32.42% of the IDA credit and 34.08% of the IDA grant (p. 15).

Key issues: grid connections lag because Umeme's concession ended in March 2025 and connection-material procurement was delayed, while off-grid results-based financing is oversubscribed. Three restructurings followed: October 2025 (US$10 million moved to off-grid financing), June 2026 (CTF grant closing extended to June 2027) and August 2026 (a further US$20 million moved to off-grid, clean cooking and productive-use schemes and the credit facility, with revised targets such as 1,600,200 connections) (restructuring paper RES02060, pp. 1, 4-5).
Status labels: progress figures are from the latest disclosed ISR, not the project's current internal status.
